uses.quote: You can use AI tools to assist you in your studies in a way which best suits your needs and discipline, as long as you do it in an ethical and considered manner.
You are allowed to use AI tools to create summaries, ask specific questions to avoid skim-reading and find relevant references and materials to guide your exploration of a subject.

You are allowed to use appropriate AI tools to help you find relevant books, articles and online resources on your topic.

uses.quote: You cannot and must not simply prompt an AI tool to deliver you with the relevant research on a subject, and include this 'generated' material in your work.

uses.quote: You can use integrated tools like Microsoft Editor, or a specialised tool, like Grammarly (not including the Grammarly Generative AI Assistant), to check for grammar, spelling and readability.
You cannot ask a Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) tool to create text for you or allow it to rewrite, expand or change beyond recognition your own text.

You can use AI tools to support quantitative data analysis, including coding support and complex data analysis.

You cannot and must not simply prompt an AI tool to write on the topic of your assignment.
For this assessment, you can use Generative AI to support you in structuring your submission, including creating a draft argument structure, identifying parts and headings, etc.
This means that you can write a paragraph and then ask an AI tool to check its structure.
You cannot and must not simply prompt an AI tool to write on the topic of your assignment.
For this assessment, you can use Generative AI to check your own text/creation for grammatical and syntactical mistakes, including getting suggestions to rephrase your work.
You cannot ask a GAI tool to create text for you or allow it to completely rewrite, expand or change beyond recognition your own text.
You cannot ask a GAI tool to create text for you or allow it to completely rewrite, expand or change beyond recognition your own text.
It is important to remember that you can only use your own notes and ideas, rather than the notes or ideas of others.
you can use AI to transform your ideas from your voice to text.
You cannot and must not simply prompt an AI tool to write on the topic of your assignment.
The use of AI in any or part of any project is entirely at the discretion of the Module Leader.

You are permitted to use industry-standard tools that utilize AI technology, such as those found in Adobe Creative Cloud, as part of your digital editing workflow. You do not need to cite this use when using these tools to make minor modifications to your own images.
You must not include, present, or submit any AI generated asset or outcome as your own.
Where generative AI is used to produce code for assessed work, you must be specific about what was produced by the AI, what changes you made to it, and what you wrote yourself.
You can ask generative AI specific questions which inform the development of your code, or aid in your understanding of the topic.

It is appropriate to use generative AI to create boilerplate code, or to generate solutions to trivial sub-problems. You should avoid using generative AI to trivialise significant components of the work you have been required to undertake.
These tools are broadly comparable with static code analysis tools, and are permitted – however you must again be transparent about their use.
You cannot and must not simply prompt an AI tool to write code on the topic of your assignment.
In either instance, these tools should be used judiciously and with caution.
For this assessment, you are not allowed to use any type of Generative AI support. This includes research support, structure support, writing/proofreading support and creative support.
